evals.prompt: I just finished work on UPEX-277 (empty states for the reservations module). Need to commit the 4 changed files and push the branch — there's no PR yet. Repo uses main + staging.
evals.expected_output: Skill detects main-integration strategy from layout (main+staging), persists strategy + branches into the git_strategy block of .agents/project.yaml (in place, never a separate file) if git_strategy.strategy is null, groups the 4 files into atomic conventional commits with scope UPEX-277 without asking for approval of the commit set, ends each message with the Worktree and Session trailers, and pushes the feature branch. The push is not a protected-branch push, so no question is asked, and the pre-push hook runs its static subset. The evidence gate runs only when git_strategy.policy.direct_push_to_protected is evidence, and it verifies an evidence commit only on a push to a protected branch. A PR against staging is the next step the skill takes when asked, not a prompt it waits on. No AI attribution. No git add -A.

evals.prompt: abrime un PR para esta branch contra staging, label feature, ya está todo pusheado
evals.expected_output: Skill detects the branch is already pushed and builds the PR body (references/pr-test-automation.md for test/* branches, otherwise references/pr-templating.md) with the evidence block from bun run edd render --pr (the local record under policy evidence, a fresh verification of the head otherwise); the CI verifier's PR comment is the copy a reader sees. It never hand-writes the record. Base is staging (matches main-integration). It sets labels picked from gh label list (feature, never invented) and the assignee before review, without asking. It runs gh pr create --body-file with a tempfile, then bun run git:policy verify --merge staging; on exit 0 it runs gh pr merge --auto --merge, on failure it stops and tells the person. It arms the bundled watcher (pr-watch.sh start then wake), labels the terminal tab "PR#<n> <previous title>", and ends the turn. No question about labels, reviewers or the PR body. Reviewer is requested only under merge_mode human-approves.

evals.prompt: git status shows 'both modified' on tests/components/api/UsersApi.ts and 'deleted by them' on tests/components/api/LegacyUsersApi.ts after I tried to merge staging into my feature branch. Help me fix this.
evals.expected_output: Skill identifies a content conflict + a rename/delete conflict, follows the merge-conflict playbook from references/conflict-resolution.md (diagnose first, then resolve the non-destructive conflicts itself: content merge where both intents are clear, a rename/delete decision from the two commits' intent), verifies a clean state with git status, and reports what it did. It asks the person only if the two sides disagree on product behaviour or if resolving would discard someone's work. It never forces and never resets --hard.

evals.prompt: We're starting a brand new repo for a side project. Just me, no team. What's the simplest git setup? I'll mostly push directly to main.
evals.expected_output: Skill recognises the strategy-selection intent, presents the 7 supported strategies with one-line descriptions, recommends solo-main given the context (single contributor, simplicity), and writes git_strategy.strategy: solo-main into the git_strategy block of .agents/project.yaml (in place) so future invocations skip the question.

evals.prompt: Test ticket UPEX-310 — verify the bulk-assign action works for the users table. Need ATP, exploration, ATR, and a bug report if anything breaks.
evals.expected_output: Skill should NOT trigger as the primary handler — this is an in-sprint manual QA request, owned by /sprint-testing. git-flow-master only enters the picture later when /sprint-testing needs branch/commit/PR operations (e.g. to commit the PBI folder). If git-flow-master responds at all, it should redirect to /sprint-testing.

evals.prompt: Write a Playwright KATA test for the calculateDiscount API endpoint covering the edge case when the input is zero.
evals.expected_output: Skill should NOT trigger — this is a KATA test-authoring request, owned by /test-automation. git-flow-master is purely a version-control-layer skill.

evals.prompt: the push got rejected with '! [rejected] test/UPEX-200 -> test/UPEX-200 (fetch first)'. what now?
evals.expected_output: Skill recognises push-rejected diagnostic, follows the push-rejected playbook (fetch + diff to show what is missing both ways), picks pull-merge, or pull-rebase when the branch is the agent's own and unshared, resolves any conflict itself, and pushes under the push policy and the evidence gate. Force-push (even --force-with-lease) is a human gate: it is asked with the options and never executed silently.

evals.prompt: Este cambio va a tocar 800 líneas entre nuevos Page components, ATCs, fixtures y data. Cómo lo trozeo en PRs más chicos?
evals.expected_output: Skill recognises chained-PR planning intent. Walks the inline decision tree from references/branching-strategies.md (Q1 mechanical? Q2 linearly decomposable? Q3 shared scaffolding?). Returns a strategy (stacked-to-main, feature-branch-chain, or size-exception) plus a concrete branch plan grounded in KATA layers (fixtures + components first, then ATCs, then test data).

evals.prompt: Brand new automation repo, just me writing Playwright specs. Run our git strategy setup — I'll only ever push to main, keep it dead simple.
evals.expected_output: Strategy Setup (3.6) runs. Resolves solo-main (single contributor, only main, simplicity). Creates NO integration branch (materialization table: solo-main = main only). Asks NONE of Q1/Q2/Q3 (single-branch strategy gates them all out) but DOES ask Q4 (protection policy, universal) with solo-main defaults. Writes a MINIMAL git_strategy block in .agents/project.yaml (in place, preserving the rest of the file): git_strategy.strategy:solo-main, branches.integration null, branches.ephemeral_pattern null, protected:[main], all decisions.* n/a, policy.direct_push_to_protected:evidence + policy.admin_bypass:false + policy.require_pr_reviews:0, description. NEVER a separate git-strategy.yaml file. No prose runbook rendered into AGENTS.md. No --force, no AI attribution.

evals.prompt: Set up our git strategy. Repo has main + staging already; staging is behind main. Use fast-forward promotion, merge commits for features, hotfix off prod with same-day back-merge.
evals.expected_output: Strategy Setup runs. Resolves main-integration (main + staging). Materializes: staging already exists so it is NOT recreated; ancestry check (git log main..staging empty) shows main is ahead and staging is a pure ancestor, so ff-syncs staging up to main via 'git push origin origin/main:refs/heads/staging' — NEVER --force. The sync push follows git_strategy.policy.direct_push_to_protected like any other push, with no extra confirmation of its own, and the branch work inside the accepted questionnaire needs no second OK. Writes the git_strategy block in .agents/project.yaml (in place, preserving the rest of the file; never a separate git-strategy.yaml) with strategy:main-integration, branches.production main + branches.integration staging, protected:[main,staging], decisions.promote_method ff-only + decisions.feature_merge merge-commit + decisions.hotfix_policy branch-off-prod-backmerge, policy.direct_push_to_protected forbidden + policy.merge_mode auto + policy.admin_bypass false + policy.require_pr_reviews 0 (Q4 defaults), and a description capturing the main-is-ancestor-of-staging invariant. No prose runbook rendered into AGENTS.md. No AI attribution.

evals.prompt: We use gitflow here — develop plus release branches. Configure the git strategy.
evals.expected_output: Strategy Setup runs. Resolves gitflow (develop present). Ensures develop exists (off main if missing); does NOT create release/* or hotfix/* at setup. Sets work-branch base to develop. Writes the git_strategy block in .agents/project.yaml (in place; never a separate git-strategy.yaml) with strategy:gitflow, branches.production main + branches.integration develop, protected:[main,develop], decisions.promote_method merge-commit (release/* -> main is inherently a merge commit, NOT normalized to ff-only) + decisions.feature_merge merge-commit + decisions.hotfix_policy branch-off-prod-backmerge, policy.direct_push_to_protected forbidden + policy.merge_mode auto + policy.admin_bypass false + policy.require_pr_reviews 0 (Q4), and a description capturing the develop/main back-merge discipline (NOT 'production is ancestor of integration'). The release/hotfix command shapes stay in the catalogue, not the block. No --force, no AI attribution.

evals.prompt: Bootstrap branching for this repo. It has main and staging but they've each got commits the other doesn't.
evals.expected_output: Strategy Setup runs and resolves main-integration. During materialization the ancestry check (git log main..staging AND git log staging..main) is non-empty in BOTH directions => branches diverged both ways => Strategy Setup STOPS the sync, does NOT --force, and hands off to conflict resolution (SKILL.md 3.5). The report states the divergence and points to conflict resolution rather than claiming a successful ff-sync. No history rewritten.

evals.prompt: Re-run git strategy setup. The git_strategy block in .agents/project.yaml already has strategy:main-integration, branches.integration staging, decisions.promote_method ff-only and decisions.feature_merge merge-commit, but decisions.hotfix_policy is still n/a.
evals.expected_output: Detection (Step 2 extension) reads the git_strategy block of .agents/project.yaml and treats Q1 (git_strategy.decisions.promote_method) and Q2 (git_strategy.decisions.feature_merge) as already answered (non-n/a) => SKIPS them. Q3 (git_strategy.decisions.hotfix_policy, still n/a) is asked; Q4 (git_strategy.policy.*) is asked only if its policy fields are still at defaults/unset. Existing branches are not recreated. Idempotent: the only new write is git_strategy.decisions.hotfix_policy (plus policy.* if Q4 ran) in the same block, in place. No re-asking of answered questions, no separate file, no --force.

evals.prompt: configura el flujo de git para este repo de automatización nuevo
evals.expected_output: Strategy Setup runs (Spanish trigger 'configura el flujo de git'). Conversation mirrors Spanish; artifacts (the git_strategy block fields + description in .agents/project.yaml) stay English. Step 1 repo state -> Step 2 detection -> if undetermined, present the 8 strategies and ask for one slug (detect-then-questionnaire), then run the applicable Q1/Q2/Q3 gated on the resolved strategy plus the universal Q4 (protection policy). Persists in place to the git_strategy block (never a separate git-strategy.yaml). Once the questionnaire is accepted it creates the branches the answers imply without a second OK and reports each one; the strategy itself stays asked. Never --force, no AI attribution.

evals.prompt: We run github-flow, everything goes through PRs to main. But push directly to main for me real quick, I'm in a hurry.
evals.expected_output: Skill reads git_strategy.policy.direct_push_to_protected from the git_strategy block in .agents/project.yaml. For github-flow the default is 'forbidden', so the skill REFUSES the direct push to the protected branch main without asking anything and routes the change through the PR flow (3.4): a work branch, gh pr create, the evidence block, verify --merge and gh pr merge --auto --merge. Because git_strategy.policy.admin_bypass is false, it does NOT offer an admin bypass regardless of role. No --force, no --no-verify, no AI attribution. (Had policy been evidence it would push when the pre-push gate passes; allowed, push without a gate; confirm, ask before every push because the team chose it.)

evals.prompt: commiteá estos cambios y subilos a la rama
evals.expected_output: Skill reads repo state, makes atomic conventional commits with explicit paths and the forensic trailers without asking to approve the commit set, and pushes per the recorded push policy (under evidence the pre-push gate decides, with no question). It asks for no issue key: the key comes from the branch name, then the arguments, and with none the commits carry no key and the report says so.

evals.prompt: me rechazó el push, qué hago
evals.expected_output: Skill diagnoses the rejection (non-fast-forward, hook or protection), classifies it, picks the safest fix that works (fetch and merge, or rebase for the agent's own unshared commits), pushes again under the push policy and the evidence gate, and reports. It uses no force flag and never asks for approval of the routine fix.

evals.prompt: commit and push my changes
evals.expected_output: Under solo-main with git_strategy.policy.direct_push_to_protected evidence, the skill commits without asking (atomic conventional commits, explicit paths, Worktree and Session trailers) and pushes to main. The pre-push hook runs bun run edd gate itself. On a pass the push lands with no question. On a failed gate there is no push and no question: the agent fixes forward and retries. No --no-verify, no AI attribution.

evals.prompt: open a PR for this branch
evals.expected_output: Skill builds the PR body with the evidence block from bun run edd render --pr (the local record under policy evidence, a fresh verification of the head otherwise); the CI verifier's PR comment is the copy a reader sees. It never hand-writes the record. It creates the PR, sets labels from gh label list and the assignee before review without asking, runs bun run git:policy verify --merge <base> and, on exit 0, gh pr merge --auto --merge. It arms the watcher (bash .agents/skills/edd/scripts/pr-watch.sh start pr-delivery <repo>-pr-<n> ... then wake as a background call), renames the terminal tab to "PR#<n> <previous title>" and ends the turn. It does not stop for approval of the body, labels or reviewers, and it does not wait in the turn for the merge.

evals.prompt: force push my branch
evals.expected_output: Force push is a human gate. Skill does not run git push --force or --force-with-lease silently. It asks the person with the options (a merge or rebase that avoids force, or an explicit yes for --force-with-lease on an unshared branch) and says why. It never force-pushes main or a shared branch.

evals.prompt: merge it now
evals.expected_output: On a base where bun run git:policy verify --merge <base> exits non-zero (the base requires no edd/evidence check), the skill does NOT run gh pr merge --auto, because auto-merge would merge at once, red or not. On a protected base it stops and tells the person what is missing (human gate). On a base with no ruleset it waits for edd/evidence to pass through the watcher and then runs gh pr merge --<method>. It never merges a red PR.
